target_customer: AI compute buyers and sovereign datacenter developers; previously floating offshore wind developers
problem: Datacenter growth is limited by land, grid and permitting; floating offshore wind platforms are costly to build and deploy.
business_model: Platform technology supplier and developer of offshore wind plus datacenter units; commercial terms not found
product_category: Floating offshore wind and marine AI datacenter platforms

founders.name: Sam Kanner
prior_employers: Floating wind company where he met Bingbin Yu in 2014 (not named on YC page)
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: helped build 100MW+ of floating wind generation.

founders.name: Bingbin Yu
prior_employers: Floating wind company where he met Sam Kanner in 2014 (not named)
education: University of Michigan, PhD Naval Architecture and Marine Engineering
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: over 10 years in offshore wind.

founders.name: James Reeves
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: with Aikido since 2020, designed helicopters and aircraft.

competitors.name: Stiesdal Offshore
competitors.traction_then: selected for a Scottish 100 MW farm per IEEE Spectrum

technical_complexity.rationale: Marine structures, certification, turbines, power and cooling at sea. A demo platform needed ABS review and offshore fabrication.

defensibility.rationale: Patented modular design and ABS statement of maturity help, but projects are capital heavy and rivals have longer track records.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; wind rivals did not copy the datacenter pivot. Other offshore compute players appeared by 2026 (Panthalassa, HiCloud, Exascale Labs).

market_need_then: Floating wind needed lower-cost construction (Aikido One assembled in about 40 working hours, 2024-11); by 2025 AI power demand shifted the pitch toward datacenters.

identity.logo: Logo, identity and website developed by a freelance designer drawing on energy flow, waves and turbines
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and playful, e.g. 'Before we go off-world, we ought to go offshore.'

branding.community_and_virality: Coverage in Electrek, Bloomberg, TechSpot and trade press including IKEA-style flat-pack framing.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong press reach and a vivid pitch, but Aikido Security is a much larger unrelated brand with the same name.

pivots.to: Marine AI datacenters on floating wind platforms
pivots.why: YC page says it pivoted from energy to datacenters in early 2025; reason not stated, though Bloomberg 2024-11 reported US offshore wind headwinds.

outcome_analysis: Active in YC Fall 2026. Three engineering founders with floating wind experience raised a $4M seed in June 2024, built and assembled a demo platform, won ABS approval and DOE prize recognition, and pivoted to datacenters in early 2025. Capital intensity and unproven demand for ocean compute are the main risks.
notes: Seed reported as more than $4 million; recorded as 4000000. Breakthrough Energy Fellows support is mentioned on the YC page without an amount. Round predates batch by more than a month. Founding year 2022 per YC page; a 2023 article describes the company as new. Prior employer of Kanner and Yu in 2014 is not named in sources opened.
